messages:
anya: seeing a quiet but steady pileup of pending GPU pods in ap-southeast2-b. mostly tiny 0.25/0.5 GPU jobs from model-train pipelines, but they're preventing a few 8GPU jobs from scheduling
samir: ah ok. is it the usual warmpool / taint mismatch or something weirder?
anya: not warmpool this time — nodes report free GPUs but scheduler keeps binpacking tiny pods across many nodes, leaving large contiguous slots empty
donna: that sounds like anchor/affinity heuristics. did we recently roll the pod-affinity-weight change?
samir: we did tweak family-affinity scoring last week (rollout id 2026-03-affinity-2). might be interacting with fractional allocation. can you paste a couple of pod descriptions?
anya: sure — snippet of pending pod from the queue:
```
Name: train-mini-452
NodeAffinity: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: topologyKey: kubelet/hostname
GPU request: 0.25
Annotations: scheduler.alpha/redwood-anchor: "gpu-anchor-v2"
Status: Pending (0/48 nodes fit: Insufficient contiguous gpus)
```
donna: "Insufficient contiguous gpus" + anchors hints at our contiguous-slot constraint kicking in. scheduler is trying to avoid splitting a family across nodes, so it sparsely fills.
samir: can you run a quick node free layout? `kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu}\n{end}'`
anya: output (sanitized):
```
node-a:4\nnode-b:4\nnode-c:8\nnode-d:8\nnode-e:0\nnode-f:4\n```
anya: but scheduler shows lots of 0.25s placed across node-a/b/f leaving node-c/d with contiguous 8s but marked Reserved by anchors for other families. weirdly anchors contain stale family id from canary.
infra-bot: [alert] scheduler_rebalance: high_fragmentation detected in ap-southeast2-b. anomaly_score=0.78. triggered at 1767111080
mike: paging infra oncall to sanity-check reserved anchors and family leases — @oncall-infra can you check anchor lease expiry and reservation state? :phone:
samir: in the meantime we could run a one-off aggressive coalescer to defragment: `kubectl exec -n infra-tooling coalesce --region ap-southeast2-b --strategy pack-contiguous --dry-run` then non-dry-run if green.
donna: agree. also suggest short-term fallback policy: relax contiguous constraint for single-family jobs under 12h duration. lessens fragmentation pressure.
anya: i'm going to manually revoke a handful of stale anchors on node-c/d that reference old rollout ids — that should free up the 8g contiguous slots. will report back after 2m.
samir: once you free, let's trigger the coalescer dry-run, then monitor scheduling events: `kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod -w | grep -i "fit"`
anya: revoked 3 anchors on node-c/d. nodes now report contiguous 8s available. running coalescer dry-run now.
after 30s:
anya: dry-run looks good, would defragment ~14 pods and free 2x8 GPU slots.
mike: nice. schedule the non-dry-run during low traffic window? ops hours are in ~25 minutes. we can do immediate if customers are blocked.
donna: also add a telemetry alert: if >5% of cluster GPUs are unusable due to anchor reservations for >10m, auto-run coalescer in safe mode.
samir: file created: INFRA-8791 (coalescer safe mode + anchor lease expiry monitor). assigning to infra-scheduling.
anya: non-dry-run kicked — pods started scheduling into freed contiguous slots. latency improved and two 8GPU jobs scheduled. :tada:
mike: can we add a short follow-up: audit rollout that introduced affinity delta and check defaults. looks like default family-anchor TTL was set too high.
donna: yep, lower anchor TTL to 10m for non-critical families. also add a migration plan for existing long-lived anchors.
anya: will update INFRA-8791 with anchor TTL change + migration steps. closing this thread unless anyone sees regressions. :white_check_mark:"
